title: Invert Binary Tree
keyIdea: Mirroring a tree = swap every node's left and right children. Do it at the current node, then let recursion do the same for both children. Any order of visiting works, as long as every node gets swapped exactly once.

approaches.name: BFS with a queue
approaches.idea: Visit nodes level by level with a queue; swap each node's children, then queue them.
approaches.why: Each node is visited once. The queue holds at most one level, w = the widest level (up to ~n/2 in a full tree).

approaches.name: Recursion (DFS)
approaches.idea: NULL → return. Otherwise swap root->left and root->right with temp, then invertTree on both children, and return root.
approaches.why: Each node is visited once. The call stack is as deep as the tree height h: O(log n) when balanced, O(n) for a chain.

options: After root->left = root->right, the old left child would be lost

quiz.q: Does it matter if you swap before or after the recursive calls?
options: No: either way every node's children get swapped exactly once

quiz.q: Space used by the recursive version?
options: O(h): the call stack is as deep as the tree

steps: What does "invert" mean exactly? What should an empty tree return? Do you build a new tree or change this one?
Draw [4,2,7,1,3,6,9] and its mirror. What happened at each node?
Is there a slower way? (Copying into a new tree, level by level?)
"Do the same thing at every node": recursion. What is the one job per node?
Base case? What's the order: swap first, then recurse, or the other way?
Code it, saying why temp is needed.
Dry-run [2,1,3]: which calls happen, in what order, and what's the final tree?
Time and space (balanced vs a chain)? How would you check if a tree is symmetric (LC 101)?
